A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from TIM to TIMotion. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original InterHuman generation, ablation, efficiency, and motion-editing results, plus InterX results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds architecture comparisons, inference-time measurements, and an LPA frequency analysis.

M1.justification: The causal interleaving, symmetric role processing, fusion, and LPA operations remain substantially unchanged. v2 generalizes the interaction-mixing interface and adds a Mamba instantiation; a Transformer adaptation already appeared in v1 Table 3. The expanded loss and editing descriptions do not establish new training or editing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-motion generation on InterHuman and InterX and motion in-betweening on InterHuman. InterX already appears in v1's appendix. Its greater prominence and the additional architecture variants in v2 do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: InterX Table 7 expands from T2M and InterGen to include TEMOS, MDM, MDM(GRU), ComMDM, and additional published T2M/InterGen results. The earlier T2M and InterGen entries are retained as starred implementations. v2 Table 2 also adds single-person-extension controls across three mixers and a separate-modeling Mamba control. The InterHuman headline comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a systematic comparison of three temporal-modeling strategies across Transformer, Mamba, and RWKV, a normalized spectral analysis using 200 randomly sampled instances, and inference-time measurements. The earlier two-block efficiency configuration disappears. Retained training budgets, diffusion sampling settings, and the editing protocol of fixing the first and last 10% remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The limited architecture ablation in v1 Table 3 becomes the broader temporal-strategy versus mixer comparison in v2 Table 2. v2 additionally examines whether LPA suppresses high-frequency motion features through Figure 6 and a 200-instance analysis. Component and normalization/kernel ablations remain, while the two-block scaling check is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 evaluations and means with 95% confidence intervals for benchmark comparisons. No changed seed policy, repeated-training count, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is established. The new spectral sample count describes an added analysis rather than increased repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds architecture and comparator results, inference times, and spectral findings, while removing the two-block efficiency result. Retained RWKV FIDs remain 4.702 on InterHuman and 0.261 on InterX; editing FID remains 3.590. InterGen's InterHuman MM Dist changes from 4.108 to 5.108, and InterX Real Diversity changes from 9.000 to 9.734. The new spectral values have conflicting condition assignments between Section 4.4.2 and Figure 6.

T1.justification: v2 Equation (11) explicitly includes Lsimple in the overall loss, whereas v1 Equation (13) lists only regularizers despite already describing noise-prediction training. This is a limited formal correction or clarification. Other mathematical revisions largely replace RWKV background exposition with standard diffusion formulations; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from pioneering RWKV-based interaction generation to MetaMotion's temporal-modeling/interaction-mixing decomposition and a framework applicable across Transformer, Mamba, and RWKV. The abstract and introduction drop the headline claim of using 32% of InterGen's parameters and foreground both datasets. The three underlying component claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a frequency-based explanation for LPA's smoothing effect and explicitly limits demonstrated applicability by task diversity and the absence of three-or-more-person experiments in Appendix E. Appendix A also extends its superiority interpretation to MModality, although Table 7 contains higher baseline values. These are substantive additions to interpretation and qualification.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D add editing pseudocode, explicit reuse of text-to-motion weights, retrieval-pool construction, and metric sampling counts of 300 and 100. v2 also clarifies motion representation and InterX result provenance. Conversely, v1's five-block/16-head specification and explicit adaptive mixing modulation equations disappear. The code-release commitment changes from 'soon' to 'upon acceptance'; these documentation changes do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the contribution around temporal modeling across architecture families rather than first applying RWKV. It removes the dedicated RWKV applications survey, including Vision-RWKV and Diffusion-RWKV, removes FineMoGen, and adds MambaAD. Earlier methods are newly organized around single-person extension versus separate modeling.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around TIMotion and MetaMotion. The RWKV preliminary section is removed, the method is reorganized into numbered subsections, and the appendix expands into sections A–E. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond renaming and renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MetaMotion schematic and radar chart, redraws the overall architecture, removes the standalone LPA diagram, and adds the frequency plots. Tables expand and reorganize, including a timing column in Table 5. v1's editing Figure 6 survives as v2 Figure 7, with two examples additionally redisplayed in Figure 5; these are retained visuals rather than new cases.

improvement.justification: v2 Table 2 strengthens comparative support for the temporal-modeling contribution, while the editing/metric documentation and explicit limitations improve transparency. The principal retained results remain stable. These gains are tempered by removal of useful RWKV implementation details and the reversed spectral-value assignments between Section 4.4.2 and Figure 6, yielding a limited net improvement.
